youtube.title: FREDDIE PONTON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Freddie Ponton examine escalating tensions around Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East, including Saudi Arabia’s vulnerability, the strategic importance of water infrastructure and growing Western military involvement. They also discuss Britain’s support for Ukraine, the use of battlefield technology and concerns over government control of online narratives and political debate. youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Joel Robinson of Radical Investment explore why rising US bond yields matter, explaining the inverse relationship between interest rates and bond prices and the growing risks around long-duration debt. They examine warning signs emerging in AI-related debt markets, the disconnect between bonds and shares, and lessons from previous market cycles, while Joel discusses ways investors can reduce exposure to potential volatility and remain focused on long-term strategy. youtube.title: VICTOR BILLOT
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with Victor Billot, president of the Alliance Party, back on the ballot after re-registering in 2024, about the party's pitch to the working class ahead of the 2026 election. He outlines plans to tax wealth rather than income, a KiwiWorks jobs programme aimed at restoring full employment and public ownership of the electricity system. For more on the Alliance Party or find them on Facebook , Instagram and YouTube For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: SUE GREY
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with Sue Grey, leader of the NZ Outdoors and Freedom Party and candidate for West Coast-Tasman, about direct democracy, decentralising decision-making and giving communities greater control. Sue outlines her party’s approach to local decision-making, individual rights, self-sufficiency and government accountability, while Maree challenges her on electoral strategy, the party’s prospects and how it could build influence beyond the election. For more on the party visit NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party or find them on X Follow Sue on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Election campaign launches, shifting political personas and the battle for key electorates dominate the conversation between Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart. They discuss National and Labour’s campaign strategies, Chris Hipkins’ new political style, Winston Peters’ enduring appeal and parliamentary standards such as the controversial behaviour in the House. youtube.title: JASON HERRICK
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Jason Herrick, Southland Federated Farmers president and NZ First candidate for Southland, about the issues facing rural New Zealand. They discuss youth crime, council reform, farming regulation, the future of New Zealand-owned food brands, energy costs and the economic potential of the lower South Island, with Jason arguing that the region needs a stronger voice in Wellington. For more on Jason Herrick or find him on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: JILL OVENS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with Jill Ovens, co-leader and national secretary of the Women's Rights Party, about the party's push for visibility ahead of the 2026 election. Jill discusses recent wins like Parliament flying a suffrage flag, the party's stance on sex-based rights and single-sex spaces, disappointment with both major blocs and plans to sit on the crossbenches and vote issue by issue if the party crosses the 5% threshold. For more from the Women's Rights Party For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: MEAGAN MCNAMARA
youtube.summary: Meagan McNamara questions Nicky Hager’s credibility as an investigative journalist, examining his account of the 2022 Parliament occupation against her own experience and thousands of hours of footage and photos from Freedom Village. She asks why Hager didn’t investigate what he encountered for himself — and challenges him to apply the same scrutiny to official Covid-19 decisions affecting more than 311,000 New Zealand teenagers.
